chunks: And He left among you what the Prophets left among their peoples,
because they did not leave them untended, without a clear path or a standing ensign.

The Book of your Lord [among you:] clarifying its permissible and forbidden matters, its obligations and virtues, its abrogating and abrogated verses, its concessions and compulsory rulings, its specific and general ones, its lessons and parables, its long and short ones, its clear and obscure ones, explaining its abbreviations and clarifying its obscurities.
ai.seo_question: How does the Quran serve as a complete guide left by the Prophets?
ai.summary: In this passage, Imam Ali (AS) positions the Quran as the enduring intellectual and spiritual legacy of the Prophets, ensuring the community remains guided without ambiguity. He details its comprehensive nature, highlighting its ability to distinguish between the clear (muhkam) and the allegorical (mutashabih), as well as abrogating and abrogated verses, thereby serving as a complete source for both legal rulings and theological wisdom. This underscores the Shia view of the Quran as a self-sufficient guide that complements the role of the Ahl al-Bayt in interpretation.

en.sayed-ali-raza: The Holy Qur’ān and Sunnah : But the Prophet left among you the same which other Prophets left among their peoples,
because Prophets do not leave them untended (in dark) without a clear path and a standing ensign,

namely the Book of your Creator clarifying its permission and prohibitions, its obligations and discretion, its repealing injunctions and the repealed ones, its permissible matters and compulsory ones, its particulars and the general ones, its lessons and illustrations, its long and the short ones, its clear and obscure ones, detailing its abbreviations and clarifying its obscurities.
